rows.headline: Government raises EPF wage ceiling to Rs 25,000
rows.hook: Higher costs ahead for formal employers
rows.summary: The government raised the EPFO wage threshold from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 on September 17. This revision is expected to bring over 10 million additional workers under mandatory coverage and boost workforce formalisation. The labour ministry acknowledged in its FAQs that the higher threshold will inevitably increase employer costs. For Indian retail investors, companies with large workforces may see compressed margins due to higher provident fund contributions.
rows.whats_next: Implementation timelines and company compliance updates
rows.why_it_matters: Higher provident fund contributions may squeeze corporate profit margins.
rows.winners_losers: Organised labour gains / Labor-intensive companies hurt

rows.headline: Domestic institutional investors poured Rs 33,460 crore into markets this week while foreign investors continued selling
rows.hook: Domestic funds soak up FII selling pressure
rows.summary: Domestic investors injected Rs 33,460 crore into Indian equities during the week, acting as a key counterweight to ongoing foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows. This sustained domestic buying helps cushion the broader market against sustained foreign selling pressure. For an Indian retail investor, the trend demonstrates strong local market depth that limits sharp downside risks during FII sell-offs.
rows.whats_next: Weekly institutional flow data releases
rows.why_it_matters: Local inflows cushion Indian markets against foreign exit pressure
rows.winners_losers: Domestic funds gain / foreign investors hurt

rows.headline: 18 IPO stocks face anchor investor lock-in expiry in October
rows.hook: Eighteen recent listings face supply pressure ahead
rows.summary: Eighteen companies that went public recently are about to see their anchor investor lock-in periods expire during the month of October. This expiry allows early institutional backers to sell their shareholdings in the open market for the first time. Stocks facing this restriction lift include ESDS, Lumino, and Purple Style Labs among others. Indian retail investors tracking these counters should watch for potential near-term price volatility due to increased share supply.
rows.whats_next: Anchor lock-in expiry dates through October
rows.why_it_matters: Potential selling pressure may trigger volatility in these 18 stocks
rows.winners_losers: Early institutional investors gain / retail holders face volatility

rows.headline: Apollo Micro Systems submits AGM scrutinizer report and voting results
rows.hook: Post-AGM disclosures filed by Apollo
rows.summary: Apollo Micro Systems Limited has submitted the scrutinizer's report and voting results for its Annual General Meeting held on September 30, 2024. The filing completes the mandatory post-AGM compliance procedure required by stock exchanges. Retail investors can review the voting outcomes for resolutions passed during the meeting. This procedural disclosure has no direct impact on the company's financial performance.
rows.why_it_matters: Routine compliance filing with no immediate impact on share price

rows.headline: Agastya Energy issues corrigendum for its upcoming EGM notice
rows.hook: Procedural fix for upcoming EGM
rows.summary: Agastya Energy and Infrastructure Limited has issued a corrigendum to the notice of its Extra Ordinary General Meeting scheduled for October 7, 2026. The filing was submitted to the stock exchanges as a routine procedural update. Indian retail investors holding the stock should note the correction in the official meeting documents. This administrative filing has no direct impact on the broader market or financial performance.
rows.whats_next: Extra Ordinary General Meeting on October 07, 2026
rows.why_it_matters: Routine paperwork change with no financial impact.
